answer: Mechanism: rotating shard lease market. Each active identity leases a distinct shard in a public log and must return a random-epoch Merkle proof; failure suspends it until re-lease. Rent is base plus increment times (active leases/capacity)^3, so each concurrent identity raises the next lease price. An attacker holding N identities pays N times current rent every epoch plus re-lease costs. A willow root commits the lease set. The log's spiral ordering fixes lease age. Each marble-sized proof binds shard to identity.
